findings.issue_text: In src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py, the first except Integration.DoesNotExist advances the pipeline without verifying installation ownership, allowing any authenticated GitHub user supplying an installation ID to bypass the sender check and link the installation to their Sentry organization before the webhook creates its database record.

goldens.comment: Null reference if github_authenticated_user state is missing
OAuth state uses pipeline.signature (static) instead of a per-request random value

The code attempts to access integration.metadata[sender][login] without checking for the existence of the sender key. This causes a KeyError for integrations where the sender metadata was not set during creation

adjudication_records.issue_text: In src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py, the first except Integration.DoesNotExist advances the pipeline without verifying installation ownership, allowing any authenticated GitHub user supplying an installation ID to bypass the sender check and link the installation to their Sentry organization before the webhook creates its database record.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a security issue. Looking at the diff, when `Integration.DoesNotExist` is caught (lines 488-489), the code calls `pipeline.next_step()` without any ownership verification. The sender check (lines 497-502) only happens in the else branch when the integration already exists. This means if an attacker supplies an installation_id before the webhook creates the Integration record, they can advance through the pipeline and potentially link the installation to their organization, bypassing the sender verification that was intended to prevent this attack.
